item.title: Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry
item.description:
Forty-three people rescued and early death toll stands at five after blaze aboard MV ‌June Aster in waters off Coron, Palawan, says coast guard Five people were confirmed dead ⁠in early counting and more than 80 were missing after a ferry caught fire ⁠off Palawan island in the western Philippines on Wednesday night, the Philippine coast ⁠guard said. Forty-three people were rescued from the MV ‌June Aster in waters off Coron, Palawan, the coast guard said. Footage showed flames engulfing parts of the vessel and responders placing victims ‌in body bags. Continue reading...

item.title: Spain’s spy agency warned of mass crossings into Ceuta before border crisis
item.description:
The EU on Wednesday said it was granting Spain 115 million euros ($130 million) in emergency aid to help bolster border security and assist returns after the massive migrant rush into the north African exclave. More than 70,000 migrants crossed into Spanish territory from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented rush that left scores dead, most by drowning as they tried to swim around a breakwater. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Missouri’s voting maps saga reaches supreme court after conflicting rulings
item.description:
Appeal against federal panel’s approval of Trump-backed maps is latest move in legal back-and-forth spanning four courts A high-stakes legal battle over Missouri’s congressional map returned on Wednesday to the US supreme court, after a series of conflicting decisions threw the state’s elections into turmoil less than two months before the November midterm elections. On Wednesday, a federal appeals court panel declined to block a ruling ordering Missouri to use the newly drawn congressional lines backed by Donald Trump to give Republicans an edge in the midterms elections. Opponents of the state’s redistricted map immediately filed an appeal to the US supreme court. Continue reading...

item.description:
Missiles launched from Iran and interceptions by Jordanian air defense systems are visible in the night sky from Damascus after Iran targeted U.S. bases in Jordan on Sept. 9, 2026. —Izz Aldien Alqasem—Getty Images Oil prices soared above $100 a barrel again Wednesday for the first time since July as the U.S. and Iran exchanged tit-for-tat strikes amid renewed hostilities. A spokesperson for the Jordanian Armed Forces said a barrage of “20 ballistic missiles” had been launched towards its territory in the early hours. item.title: Seahawks pick off Patriots’ Maye three times to stage comeback in Super Bowl rematch
item.description:
Backup quarterback engineers late Seattle rally Seahawks intercept Drake Maye three times in fourth Sam Darnold exits opening drive with hip injury Backup quarterback Drew Lock led two late scoring drives and the Seattle Seahawks intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to overcome an early injury to starter Sam Darnold and beat the New England Patriots 13-10 on Wednesday night in a Super Bowl rematch. The Seahawks were held to just a field goal through three quarters as Lock and the offense struggled to move the ball after Darnold injured his hip on the opening drive. Continue reading...

item.title: Gauff beats Andreeva to reach US Open semifinals in comeback win
item.description:
Coco Gauff saved two match points to set up a semi-final against Elena Rybakina, who secured the world No 1 ranking with her three-set win over Zheng Qinwen Rybakina has won four of her five meetings with Zheng, including two three-set victories this year . But Zheng was earlier in her comeback from elbow surgery then, the 2024 Olympic champion is a totally different proposition now, carrying the momentum of seven successive match wins in New York having come through qualifying - and the belief she can turn around any deficit after coming from 5-0 down in sets against both Madison Keys in the third round and Iga Swiatek in the last 16. Here come Zheng and Rybakina , Zheng stepping on to court wearing headphones, not that there’s much noise to drown out yet at 11.35am New York time. Both already look extremely focused with their game faces on. Continue reading...

item.title: U.S. Postal Service Failed to Properly Handle Some Ballots During This Year’s Primary Elections, Audit Finds
item.description:
Mail-in ballots sit in trays before being sorted at the Santa Clara County Registrar of Voters office in San Jose, California, on Oct. 13, 2020. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Some U.S. Postal Service facilities failed to properly handle ballots during this year’s primary elections, according to a new audit from the agency’s Office of Inspector General. Election experts say the findings call into question the agency’s ability to meet even greater demands for the November election that are under consideration by the U.S. Supreme Court. The audit, which is dated Sept. 4 but has not been previously reported, found a lack of training for post office staff on how to properly and expeditiously handle mail ballots, deficiencies in how ballots were tracked and errors leading to delays, all of which risked ballots having incorrect postmarks or otherwise arriving late to election officials, which…

item.title: Lawmakers blast AI companies after researcher warns of human extinction by 2030
item.description:

item.title: US announces $45m in security funding, additional naval vessels for Ecuador
item.description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that Washington would seek $45 million in additional security funding for Ecuador and provide military equipment as the two countries deepen cooperation against drug trafficking. During a visit to Quito, Rubio also announced new sanctions and a terrorist designation.
